portal.title: Schools Portal
portal.intro: Kinds of schools, organised several ways at once — by stage, by funding, by style, by location and by scope.

areas.desc: Who pays and who may attend
Whom the program is designed for

items.title: Preschool
items.desc: Early-childhood education before compulsory school, usually for ages 3–5, built around play and early social skills.

items.title: Pre-kindergarten
items.desc: A program in the year before kindergarten that prepares four-year-olds for school routines and early literacy.

items.title: Kindergarten
items.desc: The first year of formal schooling in many systems, usually for five- and six-year-olds.

items.title: Infant school
items.desc: A school for the youngest primary pupils, typically ages 4–7.

items.title: Junior school
items.desc: A school for the older primary years, typically ages 7–11.

items.title: Primary school / Elementary school
items.desc: The first stage of compulsory education, teaching reading, writing, mathematics and other core subjects.

items.title: Middle school
items.desc: A school between elementary and high school, often grades 6–8.

items.title: Secondary school / High school
items.desc: The stage after primary education, usually for teenagers, leading to a diploma or qualifications.

items.title: Grammar school
items.desc: In several countries, an academically focused secondary school; some select pupils by examination.

items.title: Comprehensive school
items.desc: A secondary school that admits pupils of all abilities without academic selection.

items.title: Selective school
items.desc: A school that admits pupils based on academic ability, often through an entrance test.

items.title: College-preparatory school
items.desc: A secondary school focused on preparing students for university entrance.

items.title: Sixth form college
items.desc: A college for 16–19-year-olds studying for advanced qualifications before university or work.

items.title: Professional school
items.desc: Post-secondary education that prepares students for a specific profession, such as law or medicine.

items.title: Technical school
items.desc: A school that teaches applied skills in technology, trades and engineering.

items.title: Vocational school
items.desc: A school that trains students for a particular trade or career.

items.title: Community college
items.desc: A two-year public college offering associate degrees, certificates and transfer programs.

items.title: Liberal arts college
items.desc: An undergraduate college emphasizing broad study across the arts, humanities and sciences.

items.title: University
items.desc: A higher-education institution that grants undergraduate and graduate degrees and carries out research.

items.title: Graduate school
items.desc: A school within a university that awards master's and doctoral degrees.

items.title: Research university
items.desc: A university where research is a central part of its mission.

items.title: Seminary
items.desc: An institution that trains students in theology, often for religious ministry.

items.title: All-through school
items.desc: A single school that teaches pupils from the primary years through the end of secondary education.

items.title: One-room school
items.desc: A school where students of several grades learn together in one room with one teacher.

items.title: State or public school
items.desc: A school funded and run by the government, usually free to attend.

items.title: Private school
items.desc: A school funded by tuition and private sources rather than mainly by the government.

items.title: Charter school
items.desc: A publicly funded school that operates independently under a charter with its own rules.

items.title: Academy
items.desc: A term used for various schools; in England, a state-funded school run independently of the local authority.

items.title: Specialist school
items.desc: A school that emphasizes a particular subject area, such as music, science or the arts.

items.title: Magnet school
items.desc: A public school with a special focus or program that draws students from across a district.

items.title: International school
items.desc: A school that follows an international curriculum, often serving families from many countries.

items.title: Alternative school
items.desc: A school with a nontraditional curriculum or approach, often serving students not well served elsewhere.

items.title: Single-sex education
items.desc: Education in which boys and girls attend separate classes or schools.

items.title: Music school
items.desc: A school devoted to the study and performance of music.

items.title: Montessori school
items.desc: A child-centered approach with mixed-age classrooms, hands-on materials and self-directed activity.

items.title: Waldorf school
items.desc: An approach founded by Rudolf Steiner that emphasizes imagination, arts and practical work.

items.title: Laboratory school
items.desc: A school run by a university to train teachers and test new teaching methods.

items.title: Free school movement
items.desc: A movement for schools in which students take a large share in deciding how and what they learn.

items.title: Catholic school
items.desc: A school run by the Catholic Church or a Catholic organization.

items.title: Christian school
items.desc: A school whose teaching and community life are based on Christian faith.

items.title: Madrasa
items.desc: An educational institution, often associated with Islamic learning.

items.title: Yeshiva
items.desc: A Jewish educational institution focused on the study of religious texts.

items.title: Parochial school
items.desc: A private school affiliated with a religious congregation.

items.title: Boarding school
items.desc: A school where students live on campus during the school term.

items.title: Day school
items.desc: A school where students attend during the day and return home each evening.

items.title: Distance education
items.desc: Learning delivered to students who are not physically present at a school.

items.title: Homeschooling
items.desc: Education provided at home, usually by parents or tutors.

items.title: Virtual school
items.desc: A school that teaches mainly or entirely online.

items.title: Compulsory education
items.desc: The period of education that children are required by law to attend.

items.title: Continuing education
items.desc: Education for adults after their formal schooling has ended.

items.title: Gifted education
items.desc: Programs designed for students identified as gifted or talented.

items.title: Inclusive education
items.desc: Students with and without disabilities learning together in the same classrooms.

items.title: Special education
items.desc: Instruction designed to meet the individual needs of students with disabilities.
